scope: read-only current visual baseline for character-skill presentation planning

capture_method.command_mode: Godot 4.6.2, DISPLAY=:0, gl_compatibility, Dummy audio, isolated XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME
capture_method.capture_note: Existing smoke screenshots are single rendered states after selected real feedback events or deterministic fixture setup; they are not continuous cast recordings.

samples.label: B01 confirmed hit
samples.evidence: One settled 13-damage event, player and one enemy, at 1280x720.
samples.visual_read: The contact mark and 13 number are legible, but the effect is small relative to the screen; no full cast or weapon-motion arc is shown.

samples.label: B01 shield guard
samples.evidence: A projectile fully absorbed by shield; the smoke confirms no HP loss and a cyan guard cue.
samples.visual_read: The cyan ring distinguishes guard from health loss, though the small player scale makes the cue occupy little screen area.

samples.label: B01 enemy tell and party
samples.evidence: Party and enemy tell state rendered under the smoke's feedback comfort fixture.
samples.visual_read: The target's action is not immediately self-explanatory from this still; ally ornament and enemy tell compete at similar small scale.

samples.label: B01 XP pickup
samples.evidence: The smoke injects an XP gem and confirms one actual collection event.
samples.visual_read: The resulting pickup cue is subtle in the full-screen frame and difficult to distinguish from nearby transient feedback.

samples.label: B15 dense 42-target cast
samples.evidence: A deterministic 42-target confirmed damage fixture; aggregate damage is 210 and the feedback pool applies its budgets.
samples.visual_read: The aggregate total remains readable, but a dense ring of enemy silhouettes and impact accents crowds the player; this is the clearest test for protecting the player core and action target.

samples.label: B18 boss priority
samples.evidence: Boss phase feedback is raised through the common priority pool in a B18 fixture.
samples.visual_read: Boss identity and phase bar are prominent; the player's skill expression is not the focus of this capture.

strongest_current_signals: Confirmed damage is separated from full shield absorption by a different player-side tint/ring.
Crowd damage aggregates into one explicit total, while the smoke enforces a maximum of three selected contacts per cast.
Boss phase presentation has a dedicated boss visual layer and remains visible in the B18 frame.
candidate_weak_points_for_first_batch: The screenshots do not establish that a skill's source, travel path, impact point, and secondary consequence read as one causal sequence.
Light versus heavy hit distinctions are not demonstrated by this six-frame set; current sample is one plain 13-damage contact plus guard and lethal fixtures.
No captured frame demonstrates a heal, a persistent field over time, or a linked/echo skill consequence.
The dense B15 fixture makes the player and contact layer visually busy; no pixel-level red-core visibility metric is collected by this smoke.
limits: This is a current-code renderer baseline, not a user aesthetic approval.
Frames are static captures at 1280x720; they do not measure animation readability, input timing, draw-call cost, or FPS.
The B15 42-target setup is a synthetic visual stress fixture, not a claim about a typical live encounter.
The baseline does not cover every character, equipment interaction, accessibility setting, or screen size.

B01_sparse.fixture: one controlled character, one ordinary target, one boss-class target at a time; sample cast start, travel/active state, impact, and consequence for one direct skill, one shield/heal skill, and one persistent or linked effect.
checks: A viewer can point to the caster, intended target, and impact/result without relying on floating text alone.
Light and heavy confirmed hits use visibly different scale or timing while retaining reduced-flash accessibility behavior.
Shield, healing, and health damage remain distinguishable at 960x540 and 1280x720.

B12_dense.fixture: use the actual B12 encounter at its normal spawn pacing, then add a reproducible bounded stress capture with 42 nearby targets for visual load comparison.
checks: The four-world-unit red danger core remains visible; reserve its center and a small surrounding margin from opaque effect fills.
Target/impact cues are not hidden by aggregate numbers or decorative particles; preserve the existing three-contact-per-cast and six-total-number bounds unless evidence supports a change.
Peak concurrent effect counts and image-level core occlusion are recorded; no FPS claim is made unless measured on declared hardware.

B18_boss.fixture: boss windup, player skill cast, boss hit/phase transition, and any persistent/linked consequence in one repeatable encounter segment.
checks: Boss tell, player cast source, confirmed hit, and phase change remain distinguishable in a single short sequence.
Critical boss telegraph contrast and player danger-core visibility survive overlapping skill effects.
Audio/visual priority and reduced-motion/reduced-flash variants are compared without moving the timing of confirmed events.

proposed_guardrails: Keep decorative skill particles outside a protected disk centered on the player danger core; validate pixel coverage in dense captures rather than assuming sprites are transparent enough.
Give gameplay tells and confirmed hit results a higher visual priority than trails, glow, or repeated small particles.
For the first batch, retain bounded pools and report peak active instances; do not raise existing caps without a measured readability/performance reason.
Record rendering backend, viewport size, effect counts, and capture interval before making any performance statement.
performance_and_clutter_constraints_prop.measurement_status: No new effect-count or frame-time profiler was run; these are proposed acceptance controls, not measured performance results.
